scenes.title: A normal day for Leo
scenes.captureAction: Open on an all-vector night street hook (They look. They leave. Nobody knows why.), then push the camera into Leo's store as day breaks.
scenes.narration: Shoppers look around, pick things up, and then they're gone. Most shops never find out why. Meet Leo. He runs a small furniture shop in a busy city. Every day, shoppers walk by, browse a little, and leave. Leo has clues: what they looked at, what they almost bought, and how they paid. But those clues live in different places, so every campaign is a guess. Who should he reach? And what should he offer?
onScreen: They look. They leave. Nobody knows why.

scenes.title: What Market Metro is
scenes.captureAction: Introduce Market Metro as an AI commerce environment using the actual market view and Observe, Train, Test and Measure stages. Do not show ontology as the product itself.
scenes.narration: So, could AI help Leo decide? Meet Market Metro: a living, simulated city where AI agents observe shoppers, train models and test marketing campaigns. Then we measure what changed: purchases, merchant contribution and PayPal payment outcomes.
onScreen: A commerce world for AI agents

scenes.title: The right data for the question
scenes.captureAction: The ontology routes recommendation and inquiry history separately, while distinguishing input features from later outcome labels.
scenes.narration: First, the data needs meaning. Our ontology connects shoppers, products, contacts and payments, so every prediction learns from the right examples. Recommendations and inquiries never get mixed up. And one strict rule: earlier signals can be inputs, but later outcomes are kept for labels and evaluation.

scenes.title: From understanding to action
scenes.captureAction: Recurring illustrated characters and connected actions, with saved app recordings for technical and payment evidence.
scenes.narration: Now the planner agent gets to work. It studies demand and available stock, picks twenty eight days of history, and asks local tools to train two candidate models. Every decision, tool call and result becomes a checkpoint you can open.

scenes.title: Test before sending
scenes.captureAction: Recurring illustrated characters and connected actions, with saved app recordings for technical and payment evidence.
scenes.narration: But nothing ships on a hunch. The verifier tests both models in matching development markets, checking PayPal and merchant outcomes side by side. Only a tested winner is published; otherwise, the current policy stays.

scenes.title: The recommendation becomes a purchase
scenes.captureAction: Recurring illustrated characters and connected actions, with saved app recordings for technical and payment evidence.
scenes.narration: Day thirty five. A recommendation reaches our quiet shopper, sixteen days after their last purchase. They buy a ninety six dollar side table, and it arrives the next day. Under fixed rules, that same request went unfilled.

scenes.title: A payment you can trace
scenes.captureAction: Recurring illustrated characters and connected actions, with saved app recordings for technical and payment evidence.
scenes.narration: And the money leaves a trail. PayPal Sandbox captures that exact order: ninety six dollars gross, the provider fee and the merchant's proceeds. Each record links back to the warehouse order, so the proof is traceable without double counting.

scenes.title: What changed
scenes.captureAction: Show fixed 627 vs agent 643, sixteen highlighted payment icons, and incremental payment volume, merchant contribution and modeled PayPal net.
scenes.narration: So, what changed? Across the same market, sixteen more purchases were completed and kept. Payment volume grows by two thousand three hundred forty-five dollars. Merchant contribution and modeled PayPal net both rise, even after AI cost. Every number is measured against the same fixed rules.

scenes.title: Follow the full trail
scenes.captureAction: Recurring illustrated characters and connected actions, with saved app recordings for technical and payment evidence.
scenes.narration: Don't take our word for it. AG Grid lets judges inspect the entire journey: trained models, agent decisions, campaign outcomes and the native PayPal receipt. Open any checkpoint and follow the evidence.

scenes.title: Agentic commerce that learns
scenes.captureAction: Recurring illustrated characters and connected actions, with saved app recordings for technical and payment evidence.
scenes.narration: For merchants like Leo, those two questions now have tested answers. Market Metro. Agentic commerce that learns, tests its ideas, and shows its work.

uploadDraft.title: Market Metro | Agentic Commerce That Learns | PayPal AI Hackathon
uploadDraft.description:
Market Metro turns observed merchant activity into trained models, tested campaigns and traceable PayPal payments. This demo follows one saved 12-store, 600-shopper simulation from Day 1 to a recorded agent decision, purchase and native PayPal Sandbox receipt.

Against fixed rules in that same simulation: 16 more retained purchases, $1,024.86 additional merchant contribution, and $114.96 higher modeled PayPal net after estimated model cost. Merchant contribution includes inventory value. These are simulated outcomes, not actual PayPal profit. The $96 Sandbox capture is an existing order and uses fictitious funds.

Built with PayPal Sandbox, Gemini on Vertex AI, local scikit-learn models, SQLite, Three.js and AG Studio with native AG Grid, AG Charts and a custom PayPal evidence widget. The ontology feed comparison is a separate synthetic-data test.

Source and setup: https://github.com/VinceVence/market-metro
Original code: MIT. Third-party components retain their own licenses.
